task.description: WF-02 Step 4 (TEST-RUNNER) for REQ-134: run scripts/test_parallel.sh for the full default suite (AC4), and separately attempt to bring up a live Keycloak and run `mix test --include keycloak` for the real-token evidence AC1/AC2/AC3 explicitly require, quoting real output rather than relying on code review.
acceptance_criteria: a test obtains a genuine token from the running Keycloak and drives it through Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline end to end, with the real assertion output quoted
the token's signature is verified against the live JWKS via the real verifier, not TokenVerifierDouble -- demonstrated by the test failing if pointed at a tampered token
JIT provisioning creates a real user row on first authentication and reuses it on the second, asserted across two calls
the default mix test run still passes with Keycloak stopped, quoted as evidence
the real-token tests skip with a message naming exactly what must be running, rather than failing obscurely
the result states the exact command a developer runs to execute them

result.summary:
Default full suite (scripts/test_parallel.sh): N=16 (nproc) hit the documented ISS-0219/ISS-0222 host connection-spike pattern (6/16 partitions crashed with no Result: line; the 13 failures in the partitions that did report were all DBConnection.ConnectionError or contention-cascaded, none touching REQ-134's own diff files). Re-ran at TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 per the script's own inline guidance -- clean: 'combined: 1981 tests, 5 properties, 0 failures (1986/1986 passed)', all 4 partitions produced a Result: line. One partition's log confirms AC4 in the default run: 'Excluding tags: [:keycloak]' / 'Result: 522 passed (1 property, 521 tests), 3 excluded'.

Live Keycloak: not initially reachable (a stale letflow-keycloak-1 container predated the workspace's .env port setting and had no host port bound). Recreating it with --force-recreate hit a real port collision: 0.0.0.0:8092 was already bound by an unrelated, healthy, 21-hour-old sibling docker-compose project (agent-adaebfe03c52023c5-keycloak-1) -- almost certainly a concurrent sibling agent session/worktree. Per this session's own operating rule for concurrent sibling sessions (check state, decide at own discretion, do not disturb an active sibling's container, report the decision afterward): did not touch that container. Instead changed this workspace's own untracked .env (LETFLOW_KEYCLOAK_PORT 8092 -> 8093, verified free), recreated only letflow-keycloak-1 on 8093. config/keycloak_port.exs reads the same .env for both dev/test config and this compose file, so no code changed. Keycloak came up healthy with realm bpm-default imported, verified directly via curl against the OIDC discovery endpoint.

Ran `mix test --include keycloak test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` for real: Result: 2/3 passed, Failed: 1 test. AC1 and AC3 passed with real live-Keycloak evidence. AC2 ('a token with a tampered signature is rejected with 401 unauthorized', line 236-249) failed: `assert Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body) == %{"error" => "unauthorized"}` failed because the real response body is `%{"detail" => "invalid or expired bearer token", "error" => "unauthorized"}` -- conn.halted and conn.status == 401 both held; only the exact-equality body assertion failed. Root cause traced into lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's reject/4 (line 322-323, unchanged, pre-existing): it always encodes both `error` and `detail` keys on every rejection path, and the sibling test test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196 already correctly handles this with a partial pattern match. The new AC2 test's assertion is a test-code bug (too strict), not an application regression -- this defect was invisible until today because Keycloak was never reachable in this environment before this run (step3/step3b both validated AC1-3 by code review only, never by execution).

Re-confirmed AC4 with Keycloak now running: `mix test test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs` (no --include) -> 'All tests have been excluded.' / 'Result: 0 tests, 3 excluded' -- confirms exclusion is a test_helper.exs config default independent of Keycloak's runtime state.

Unblock-Everything: no pre-existing/unrelated failures found blocking this run. The N=16 crashes are the already-documented ISS-0219/ISS-0222 host-resource pattern, fully absent at the documented N=4 workaround, so not filed as new. The one real failure (AC2) is inside REQ-134's own new file, so it is this run's own responsibility, not something to attribute away.

issues.description: test/letflow/integration/keycloak_auth_pipeline_test.exs:250 (AC2's tampered-signature test) asserts full map equality `Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body) == %{"error" => "unauthorized"}` against a response body that (correctly, per lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's pre-existing reject/4) also always includes a "detail" key. Fails deterministically on any real 401 response. Fix: change to a partial pattern match, matching the established convention in test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:196 (`assert %{"error" => "unauthorized"} = Jason.decode!(conn.resp_body)`), and update test/specs/REQ-134.md's AC2 section if it documents the exact-equality shape.

result.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER -- fix AC2's overly-strict body-equality assertion per the BLOCKER above, then re-run through TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step3b) and TEST-RUNNER (step4). AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, and the full default suite (1986/1986 at TEST_PARALLEL_N=4) all PASS and do not need rework.
